paper.title: Simple Regret Minimization for Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Simple regret minimization for contextual bandits (pure exploration phase followed by pure exploitation phase)
unmapped: Each arm's expected reward f_a(x) is a function of the context in an RKHS with bounded kernel
Contexts form a (possibly non-i.i.d.) random process on a compact space, with conditional second-moment operator having d* eigenvalues above lambda_x (Assumption A III)
No feedback during the exploitation phase; simple regret is evaluated per context at each exploitation step
The learner knows lambda_x, d*, the hardness H_epsilon and the constants C_1, C_2 (used to set beta and N_lambda)
settings.definition_quote: The first \(T\) time steps belong to the \emph{exploration phase} where the learner observes context \(x_t\), chooses arm \(a_t\) and obtains reward \(r_{t}\). The time steps after \(T\) belong to an \emph{exploitation phase} where the learner observes context \(x_t\), chooses arm \(a_t\) and earns an implicit reward \(r_{t}\) that is not returned to the learner.

bound.regime: beta_c > 0, i.e. T > (16 H_epsilon C_2^2 - 2 A lambda)/lambda_x + N_lambda (A-1)

symbols.N_lambda: burn-in length max(2(1-lam)/lambda_x, d_star, 256/lambda_x^2 log(128 d_tilde/(lambda_x^2 delta)))
symbols.lambda_x: lower bound on nonzero eigenvalues of conditional second moment operator of features
symbols.d_star: dimension of the subspace containing the feature second-moment operator
symbols.H_epsilon: total hardness sum_a H_{a,eps}^{-2}, H_{a,eps} = inf_x max((Delta_a(x)+eps)/2, eps)
symbols.C_2: rho*sqrt(sum log(1+sigma_hat^2/lam)) + sqrt(lam)*||f_a||_H, O(rho sqrt(log T))

conditions: Assumptions A I-A III: contexts form a random process on a compact space; kernel bounded by L with continuous feature map and separable RKHS; conditional second moment operator has d* eigenvalues > lambda_x and zero elsewhere
f_a in RKHS for each arm
bound on probability that simple regret at any exploitation step t > T is >= epsilon, conditional on x_t
tuning: beta = sqrt((lambda_x(T - N_lambda(A-1)) + 2 A lambda)/(16 C_1^2 H_epsilon)) - C_2/C_1

source.label: thm:MainTheorem
source.quote: Consider a contextual bandit problem as defined in Section \ref{sec:formal_setting} with assumptions \ref{AsX}-\ref{Alambda}. For  \( 0 < \delta \leq \frac{1}{8} \), \( \epsilon > 0 \) and \( N_{\lambda} := \max(...) \), let \beta = \sqrt{\frac{\lambda_{x}(T - N_{\lambda}( A -1)) + 2 A\lambda}{ 16  C_1^2 H_{\epsilon} }} - \frac{C_2}{C_1}. For all \(t > T\) and \(\epsilon  > 0\), \PP (R_{\Omega(x_t)}(x_t) < \epsilon | x_t) \geq 1 - A(T - AN_\lambda) e^{-\beta^2} - A\delta.

results.notes: Recorded as the failure probability P(R >= eps | x_t). Paper's A (number of arms) mapped to K. Environment labelled stochastic_iid for the noise/reward model, but contexts are a general (possibly non-i.i.d.) random process; see unmapped. Paper says this gives order A(T-AN_lambda)exp(-(T-AN_lambda)/H_eps).
